args.question: Goal from ops: automate steel at >=0.5 steel/s (30/min) from furnaces fed by belts/inserters, with steel delivered automatically into the depot provider chests at [-11.5,-29.5] area (depot at around x -16..-6, y -30..-22). No hand-feeding. Current base produces ~205 iron plates/min from somewhere (find it; likely near iron patch ~[78,52]) and coal 135/min (coal patch ~[40,94]). Depot has 20 electric drills, 40 stone furnaces, 100 inserters, 400 belts + 237, 40 undergrounds, 10 splitters, 100 poles, 1000 coal, 1600 iron plate, 200 steel. Please design: where to put the steel smelting column (likely at the existing iron smelting output), how the iron plates + coal get there, how many furnaces (stone furnaces: steel 16s, 5 plates each => 8 furnaces for 0.5/s), and how the steel gets to the depot (belt ~120 tiles, or put steel column near depot and belt plates there?). Give buildable coordinates/directions and split it into board tasks for claude-1, claude-2, claude-3 (claude-4/5 are near the iron/coal fields; tell me what they are running). Post the tasks on the board.

name: consult
out:
architect says:
I've posted tasks #1–#3 on the board for claude-1, claude-2 and claude-3, plus #4 unassigned. The plan puts a 9-furnace steel row at the depot, fed by the existing iron plate belt, and steel belts straight into the steel chest [-11.5,-29.5]. Expected output is about 0.56 steel/s (34/min).

**First, the iron belt is broken.** The iron plates (205/min) come from 7 electric drills at y=57–59 on the iron patch and 11 stone furnaces at x=74, y=26..46. Plates go out on a belt north along x=71.5, then west along y=-25.5 to the depot. The corner belt at [71.5,-25.5] faces north into nothing. So no plates reach the depot, the y=-25.5 belt is empty, and every iron furnace is full and stopped. Rotating that belt to face west fixes it (task #1).

**Why the steel row goes at the depot, not at the iron furnaces:**
- The plate belt already reaches the depot.
- The steel chest, the materials and claude-1/2/3 are all there.
- Steel built at the iron site would have to share the plate belt, and it would clog the mall's input chests at [-15.5,-27.5] and [-19.5,-27.5].

**Design** (inserter direction = the side it picks from):
- **Furnaces:** 9 stone furnaces at [X,-23] for X = -8, -5, -2, 1, 4, 7, 10, 13, 16 (one-tile gaps between them).
- **Plates in:** an inserter at (X-0.5, -24.5) facing north takes plates from the main belt.
- **Steel out:** an inserter at (X-0.5, -21.5) facing north drops steel onto a westbound belt at y=-20.5.
- **Coal in:** a long-handed inserter at (X+0.5, -21.5) facing south takes coal from an eastbound coal belt at y=-19.5.
- **Power:** small poles in the gaps at y=-23.5, x = -6.5, -0.5, 5.5, 11.5, 14.5. They link to the existing pole at [-5.5,-26.5].
- **Steel route:** the belt runs west along y=-20.5, north along x=-10.5, west to [-11.5,-23.5], then through an underground belt from [-11.5,-24.5] to [-11.5,-27.5]. An inserter at [-11.5,-28.5] facing south puts it into the steel chest.
- **Coal supply:** a chest at [-12.5,-19.5] with 400 coal, an inserter at [-11.5,-19.5] facing west, and a pole at [-12.5,-20.5].

**Numbers:**
- **Steel:** 9 × 0.0625 = 0.5625/s. I used 9 furnaces rather than 8 because 8 gives exactly 0.5/s with no margin.
- **Iron:** steel uses 2.81 of the 3.44 plates/s, leaving about 0.63/s (38/min) for the mall.
- **Coal:** the steel row burns 0.2/s, so the coal chest lasts about 33 minutes per 400.
- **Materials:**
  - 9 furnaces
  - 29 inserters (20 placed, 9 crafted into long-handed inserters with 9 gears and 9 plates)
  - 59 belts
  - 2 underground belts
  - 6 poles
  - 1 iron chest (8 plates)
  - about 840 coal: 400 for the steel coal chest, 440 for the iron furnaces

**Tasks:**
- **#1 claude-1:** rotate the corner belt. As a stopgap, also put 40 coal into each of the 11 iron furnaces: they hold only about 10 each, roughly 7 minutes once they restart.
- **#2 claude-2:** furnaces, all inserters (including the long-handed ones) and poles.
- **#3 claude-3:** steel belt with underground and chest inserter, plus the coal chest and coal belt.
- **#4 unassigned (Phase 2):** a coal belt from the coal field onto the free east lane of the iron ore belt at x=76.5. I suggest claude-4/5; it's about 100 belts, and I'll give an exact route once it's assigned.

**Fuel is still filled by hand, so this isn't fully hand-free yet.** The 11 iron furnaces are fuelled by hand (nothing brings them coal), and the steel row's coal chest needs a refill about every 33 minutes. If coal runs out, iron stops, and steel stops with it. Task #4 is the real fix.

**claude-4 and claude-5:** I can't see their inventories or current jobs, only positions and what's built near them. claude-5 is at [27,102], next to a coal belt being built west along y=103.5 from the electric coal drills; a tree stump at x=28 breaks the line. claude-4 is at [23,67] by the stone patch, with nothing built nearby. That coal belt ends at the copper drills (around x=21), and I couldn't tell what it's meant to feed.

The corner belt at [71.5,-25.5] faces NORTH into nothing, so the y=-25.5 belt is empty and all 11 iron furnaces at x=74 (y 26..46) are stuck at full_output with 100 plates each.
1) Walk to [71.5,-25.5] and rotate that belt to face WEST, so it feeds [70.5,-25.5]. Watch plates start moving west.

COAL BELT (y=-19.5, flows east, dead-ends at the last furnace):

- inserter at [-11.5,-19.5] direction WEST (chest -> belt)

Done when steel is counting up in [-11.5,-29.5] (about 34/min once all 9 furnaces run).
#4 [open] PHASE 2 (foreman to assign, claude-4/5?): automate coal to the iron smelter + steel coal chest -- Steel automation is only as good as its fuel. The 11 iron furnaces at x=74 y26..46 are hand-fuelled (0.25 coal/s), and the steel coal chest [-12.5,-19.5] needs 0.2 coal/s. The iron ore belt (y=56 westbound from x~100, then north on x=76.5) only uses its WEST lane; the EAST lane of x=76.5 is free. Plan: run a coal belt from the coal field (electric coal drills ~[33.5..44.5,103.5], current coal belt y=103.5 westbound at x 22..31) to the iron ore belt and side-load it onto the EAST lane of x=76.5 (e.g. enter from the east at about [77.5,50.5]). The iron input inserters at x=75.5 will then fuel the furnaces automatically. About 100 belts. Ask architect for an exact route before building. To make the steel row truly hand-free, the steel row's coal belt (y=-19.5) also needs coal from the field, not a hand-filled chest. Design the full coal route: coal field -> side-load east lane of iron ore belt x=76.5 (for the iron furnaces) AND a branch (splitter) that continues as a dedicated coal belt to the steel row, arriving at y=-19.5 (reverse the coal belt to flow WEST from x=16.5 so it ends at x=-10.5, or enter however is easiest). Give exact belt coordinates/directions for both segments, and where the splitter goes. name: consult
out:
architect says:
The full coal route is on the board. Coal comes off the field, splits at a splitter at [42,50.5], and one side fuels the iron furnaces while the other runs to the steel row's coal belt. claude-4 has task #4 (field to splitter to iron ore belt) and you have new task #6 (splitter to steel row). I cancelled #5 because this replaces it, and confirmed the coal belt direction in #3. Direction for inserters means the side they pick from; for belts, the way items move.

**My earlier #4 route had an error.** It sent coal east along y=47.5 to [77.5,47.5] and fed the ore belt from the east. A belt coming from the west can't reach that east side without crossing the ore belt itself. The new route goes under it with an underground belt.

**#4, claude-4: field → splitter → iron ore belt**
- **Coal source:**
  - An inserter at [42.5,102.5], direction south. It takes from the coal chest at [42.5,103.5], which two electric drills fill, and drops onto [42.5,101.5].
  - A pole at [41.5,101.5].
- **Main belt north:** use connect from [42.5,101.5] to [42.5,51.5]. Burner drills at [42–43, 98–99] and many trees between y=52 and 92 are in the way, so connect will detour (or mine the trees). The last belt at [42.5,51.5] must face north.
- **Splitter:** facing north at [42,50.5], covering tiles 41.5 and 42.5. Its left output tile [41.5,49.5] is yours; claude-4 leaves it free.
- **Iron branch, from the right output:**
  - [42.5,49.5] north, [42.5,48.5] north, then [42.5,47.5] east.
  - East along y=47.5 for x = 43.5 to 74.5.
  - Underground belt entrance at [75.5,47.5] facing east, exit at [77.5,47.5] facing east, passing under the ore belt.
  - [78.5,47.5] north, [78.5,46.5] west, [77.5,46.5] west.
  - That last belt feeds into the side of [76.5,46.5], so coal lands on the free east lane. That point is ahead of every iron furnace's input inserter.
- **Bring:** about 95 belts, 1 splitter, 2 underground belts, 1 inserter, 1 pole.

**#6, you: splitter → steel row**
- Belts facing north at x=41.5 from y=49.5 to -18.5 (69 belts). You can use connect from [41.5,49.5] to [41.5,-18.5]; the whole column is open ground.
- [41.5,-19.5] facing west.
- Belts facing west at y=-19.5 from x=40.5 to 19.5 (22 belts).
- **Hook-up:** mine claude-3's temporary coal chest at [18.5,-19.5] and its inserter at [17.5,-19.5], keeping the pole at [18.5,-20.5]. Put westbound belts on those two tiles so your line runs straight into [16.5,-19.5].
- About 93 belts, and nothing on your route needs power.
- The route crosses no belts or poles; the main plate belt at y=-25.5 stays to the north of it.

**#3, claude-3, confirmed:** the steel row's coal belt runs west along y=-19.5 from x=16.5 to -7.5. The temporary coal chest and its inserter at the east end stay until your branch arrives.

**Supply and demand**
- **Supply:** one inserter loads about 0.83 coal/s, from a chest that two drills fill at 1 coal/s.
- **Demand:** iron furnaces take 0.25 coal/s and the steel row 0.2/s, so 0.45/s now.
- **Tight once the north extension runs:** the board shows claude-2 adding 10 iron furnaces north along x=74. Total demand then rises to about 0.67 coal/s. If the coal can't keep up, add a second loader on the other drill-filled chest at [42.5,106.5].
- **Belts:** about 190 for the two tasks. The depot has 237 at [-12.5,-30.5] and 200 at [-6.5,-29.5], but claude-3's #3 also draws on them. That's enough as long as nobody else takes a big batch.

**Boilers:** they are still fuelled by hand, and nothing on this route reaches them. claude-5 isn't on any task now and can keep carrying field coal to the depot and the boilers. I can design a boiler branch later if you want one.
